correctness.rationale: The pairwise map is exactly the neutral-utility version of the displayed microscopic equation. On the zero-sum subspace, its synchronous W2 squared contraction factor is 1-2t/(N-1), t=2mu(1-mu)>0. Stationary second moments follow by exact conditional expectation. A supposed stationary Gaussian covariance sigma^2 P cannot satisfy every pairwise conditional Gaussian covariance, because selected-pair projected noise has rank two but the required compensation rank one for N>=3; N=2 is scalar Gaussian AR(1). For N=3, the zero-sum fourth-power identity and Gaussian fourth-moment expansion produce the closed recurrence and the exact kurtosis 3(16-11t)/(16-12t). Exact rational checks have been executed from check.py. These arguments do not use finite simulations as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The natural null case of the source model is a stochastic gossip chain. At finite population it has a mathematically non-Gaussian stationary microscopic spread even when all innovations are Gaussian, affecting the Gaussian representative-agent closure used for utility-driven consensus. The result identifies N=3 as the first genuinely random-partner non-Gaussian case, gives a universal variance finite-size factor and a sharp observable fourth-moment calibration (maximal excess 3/20). N=3 is the structurally first nontrivial population rather than an arbitrary slice, and the result distinguishes centered stationarity from the unbounded opinion-mean random walk. Scope limits are explicitly stated.
